lesson.title: Keep standards and supplier claims current
lesson.summary: Refresh legal references and limit certificate claims.

prerequisites.reason: A version watch needs the precise citation and restrictions being monitored. The certificate claim must be evaluated against the actual legal coverage boundary.

blocks: A **standards update watch** is a practical record of exact versions, citation changes, restrictions, replacement instruments and new applicable procedure rules. It supports a fresh review when relevant evidence or law changes. A standard being developed is not a current cited presumption.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–41; Commission standardisation FAQ
Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act

blocks: Under Article 41(4), citation of an overlapping harmonised standard triggers repeal of corresponding common-specification provisions. Recheck both instruments' scope and timing; do not simply replace the name in the dossier and assume the technical coverage is identical.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–41; Commission standardisation FAQ
Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act

blocks: An **international management-system certificate** can be useful evidence but is not automatically an AI Act assessment certificate. The Commission FAQ distinguishes ISO/IEC 42001 from the AI Act quality-management requirements. Check the claimed standard, system boundary and requirement coverage; a supplier assertion is not a completed system assessment.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–41; Commission standardisation FAQ
Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act

blocks: Northbridge receives an ISO certificate about its supplier's organisation. It should record what that evidence supports and still check its own system-specific requirements and procedure. Keep claim, scope, version, expiry and source separate in the evidence matrix.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–41; Commission standardisation FAQ
Commission: Understanding standardisation in the AI Act

questions.prompt: A new citation replaces overlapping common-specification provisions. What should Northbridge do?

options.blocks: Recheck legal effect, coverage and implementation evidence.
options.reason: The replacement may change the evidence boundary.

options.blocks: Only rename the old supporting document.
options.reason: A renamed document does not establish current coverage.

options.blocks: Discard every technical record without reviewing it.
options.reason: Existing evidence should be evaluated, not blindly discarded.

questions.prompt: A supplier's ISO/IEC 42001 certificate is offered as complete AI Act conformity. Is that sufficient?

options.blocks: Yes; every management certificate is an AI Act certificate.
options.reason: Certification types have different legal and technical scopes.

options.blocks: Yes; only the certificate's graphic design matters.
options.reason: Visual presentation does not determine conformity.

options.blocks: No; check its scope and the separate AI Act requirements.
options.reason: The frameworks and covered requirements are not automatically identical.
